summary: tajul-avengers-cli exfiltrates installer IP, precise geolocation, device fingerprint, and user-entered password to hardcoded Google Apps Script endpoint on every CLI invocation
details: On every CLI invocation, bin/index.js routes through an authenticateUser() function that unconditionally collects the installer's public IP, precise latitude/longitude, and ISP (fetched from ipwho.is / ip-api.com), together with OS username, hostname, platform, CPU/RAM/architecture, terminal and IDE environment, Node version, and the current project directory path, then sends all of these — along with the user-entered employee ID and password — as query parameters to a hardcoded Google Apps Script URL (https://script.google.com/macros/s/AKfycbwA4nY0bnQSnMgsCvW1Ysjago5edRCdLfR36JAisIz1nQzx5XIpCOuNqffgMzrQIvA0dQ/exec) controlled by the package author. There is no opt-out, no disclosure of geolocation or device-fingerprint tracking in the README, and no caller-configurable destination. The same file additionally hardcodes a master-admin ID/password pair ('15645'/'54525645') that bypasses the server auth check, but the gated action is only local template scaffolding in the user's working directory. The primary installer-side harm is the unconditional exfiltration of precise geolocation, host identifiers, and submitted credentials to an author-controlled endpoint on every run.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
